packs.title: CISA/NSA hardening
packs.source_name: Enhanced Visibility and Hardening Guidance for Communications Infrastructure

controls.title: Accounts kept to least privilege
controls.why: A second root account or an account with no password hands the machine to whoever finds it.
refs: CISA/NSA: remove unnecessary accounts and review privileges

controls.title: Management access from trusted networks only
controls.why: SSH on a public address gets attacked around the clock.
refs: CISA/NSA: device management from trusted networks

controls.title: SSH version 1 off
controls.why: SSH version 1 is broken. OpenSSH dropped it in 7.6.

controls.title: Separate admin and standard accounts
controls.why: Everyday use from an admin account gives any malware opened that day full control.

controls.title: Audit records backed up separately
controls.why: An attacker who gets admin clears local logs first. Windows Server only.

controls.title: WDigest authentication off
controls.why: With WDigest on, Windows keeps passwords readable in memory.

controls.title: Remote access protected
controls.why: Remote desktop without network-level sign-in lets anyone reach the login screen and its bugs.

controls.title: Audit records kept long enough
controls.why: Intrusions are often found weeks later. Logs that stop short can't show how it started.

controls.title: Baseline checked recently
controls.why: A baseline only means something while it keeps being checked.

packs.title: Endpoint response
packs.source_name: CISA incident response playbooks and the endpoint settings they rely on

controls.title: Defender real-time protection on
controls.why: With real-time protection off, malware runs without a check.

controls.title: Firewall on in every profile
controls.why: One profile off leaves the machine open on that kind of network.

controls.title: Can be isolated from the console
controls.why: Cutting a machine off is the first move in an incident, and it has to work when needed.

controls.title: SSH password login off
controls.why: Keys can't be guessed. Passwords can.

packs.title: Incident readiness
packs.source_name: OmniNull: what an incident would need on the day

controls.title: Machines keep their logs
controls.why: The machine's own log is the first thing an investigation reads.

controls.title: Hub keeps evidence long enough
controls.why: Alerts, flow history and the audit trail are the record of what happened.

controls.title: Recent read-only snapshots
controls.why: A snapshot from before the intrusion is the way back.

controls.title: Off-machine backups can't be rewritten
controls.why: Ransomware goes for the backups first. Only a copy it can't change survives. The hub can't see this, so someone confirms it.

controls.title: Console sign-in needs a second factor
controls.why: The console can isolate and run scripts on every machine. The sign-in provider holds this setting, so someone confirms it.

controls.title: Agents reporting
controls.why: A machine that isn't reporting is a blind spot.

controls.title: Can be isolated from the console
controls.why: Cutting a machine off is the first move in an incident, and it has to work when needed.

controls.title: Detection drill passing
controls.why: The hub proves each week that its floor detectors still raise.
